I have been using Gentoo Linux since some some time around 2005 on various platforms, and for
different purposes.

As for myself, I have almost always trusted the default settings mentioned in the handbook, i.e. the
"conservative" `CFLAGS` parameters, using `-march=native` to optimize for the given processor
architecture, and rarely venturing further into "optimization" land.

However, throughout forums, Reddit, chat channels, and other places, there's been constant debates on
what "the best" optimization flags are (or should be), with many swearing by their magical incantations
of compilers, compiler flags, and linkers, to produce seemingly fantastic, but vague, claims of
performance gains.

I hadn't given much thought as to how my own systems should be optimized, until I got an Intel NUC,
with a 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1260P processor. This processor has differentiated performance
("P-Cores") and efficient-cores ("E-Cores") in Intel's lingo, and sometimes fail to produce binaries
that can execute on all cores with automatic `-march=native` settings. So I started digging deeper
to find out exactly what compiler flags I _should_ use on a given architecture, and which ones actually
made a difference performance-wise.

The [GCC optimization](https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/GCC_optimization) article on the Gentoo Wiki also
provided some interesting food for thought.

So how would I actually test this systematically? I set up virtual machines in [libvirt](https://libvirt.org/)
on two of my machines to find out, in general terms, what would produce the most optimized system, with
everything else (installed software, kernel versions, filesystems, schedulers, etc.) being the same.

These two machines are

  1. the previously mentioned Intel NUC12WSHi7 (M42761-303) with 64GiB of RAM, running Gentoo Linux as the
     host operating system. The NUC has an Intel i7-1260P, which is part of the
     [Alder Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alder_Lake) series of processors, with 16 cores.
  2. a [Compulab Airtop3](https://edge.compulab.com/products/airtop3/) with 128GiB RAM, also running
     Gentoo as the host OS. This particular Airtop3 has an Intel
     i7-9700, a [Coffee Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_Lake) 9th generation CPU with 8 cores.

I ended up with a set of Gentoo Linux VM:s, each with different combinations of `CFLAGS`/`CXXFLAGS`,
[hardened](https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Hardened_Gentoo)/unhardened profiles, link-time optimization
([LTO](https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/LTO)), profile-guided optimization
([PGO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Profile-guided_optimization)) (where applicable),
and [Graphite](https://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/Graphite) loop optimizations. I rebuilt all of these systems from the ground up (`emerge --emptytree`)
and kept them updated continously over a period of several months in order to properly log compile times, etc.

Optimization is usually a set of trade-off between simplicity, stability, compilation time, execution time,
and maintainability. As an example, if a program takes an extra 20 minutes to compile every time you
install or upgrade it, and the gain in performance each time you use it is measured in seconds, it might not
be worthwhile to optimize it from a technical perspective. Many, however, have a complementary -- lets call it a
_psychological_ perspective -- and derives peace-of-mind from knowing their system is optimized, and uses ALL
of their processor. So I knew I needed to be able to compare compilation times, and cross-reference them with
any performance data I could derive.

As previously mentioned, the NUC has differentiated cores, which means that the compiler cannot reliably
use `-march=native` to resolve the correct parameters for the CPU. Instead, on that platform
[resolve-march-native](https://github.com/hartwork/resolve-march-native) resolves the actual (usable)
compiler flags.

This article compares benchmark outcomes across supported operating systems, with focused analysis of
Gentoo tuning choices (`CFLAGS`, `PGO`, `LTO`, `Graphite`).

The real hostnames have been replaced by names from Greek Mythology so we can refer to them later in this
article.

The virtual machines are run on `app-emulation/libvirt-12.0.0`/`app-emulation/qemu-10.2.2` through an
Ansible-based harness that provisions and collects the benchmark data.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import os
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("../../scripts").resolve()))
from benchmarks_article_catalog import get_category_meta
from benchmarks_article_data import load_benchmark_rows
from benchmarks_cflags_analysis import enrich_gentoo_cflags_dimensions

anonymize_hosts = os.getenv("QUARTO_BENCHMARKS_ANONYMIZE", "1").lower() not in {"0", "false", "no"}
rows = load_benchmark_rows(Path("../../benchmarks/results"), anonymize_hosts=anonymize_hosts)
df = pd.DataFrame(rows)

if df.empty:
    raise RuntimeError("No benchmark rows found in benchmarks/results. Run benchmarks first.")

df["mean_s"] = pd.to_numeric(df["mean_s"], errors="coerce")
df["stddev_s"] = pd.to_numeric(df["stddev_s"], errors="coerce")
df = df.dropna(subset=["mean_s"])
```

## How the Benchmarks Are Performed

The benchmark suite is executed by the Ansible role `roles/run_benchmarks`, which prepares each VM, runs
benchmark categories, and writes raw JSON artifacts for every host. Most workloads are measured with
Hyperfine-style repeated command timing, with category outputs stored as one JSON file per category.

To reduce noise, the workflow applies a normalization/denormalization pass around benchmark execution.
This keeps host state and scheduling more consistent between runs and avoids permanent benchmark-side
changes after completion.

## How Data Is Collected

Each host writes to `benchmarks/results/<host>/`:

1. `metadata.json` with host/build context (OS, compiler flags, profile, tool versions, platform details).
2. Category result files with per-command timing data (`mean`, `stddev`, command string).
3. Optional benchmark notes where present.

This article loads those files through `scripts/benchmarks_article_data.py`, converts them to long-form
rows, applies optional hostname anonymization, and then derives aggregate comparisons (cross-OS and
Gentoo tuning-focused).

```{python}
from html import escape

import pandas as pd
from benchmarks_article_data import _translate_march_to_codename

# Extract unique Gentoo hosts and their configuration
gentoo_hosts = (
    df[df["os"] == "Gentoo"][["host", "gentoo_profile", "march_native", "pgo_enabled", "lto_enabled", "graphite_enabled", "common_flags", "cflags"]]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .sort_values("host")
)


def virtualization_host_cpu(march_native):
    if march_native == "alderlake":
        return "🧊 Alder Lake"
    if march_native == "skylake":
        return "☕ Coffee Lake"
    return "?"

def build_table_for_arch(hosts_df, arch_filter):
    """Build an HTML table for a specific architecture."""
    filtered = hosts_df[hosts_df["march_native"] == arch_filter].copy()
    if filtered.empty:
        return None

    # Sort by CFLAGS complexity (length of expanded string)
    def cflags_length(row):
        cflags_val = row["cflags"] or ""
        cflags_val = cflags_val.replace("${COMMON_FLAGS}", row["common_flags"] or "")
        cflags_val = cflags_val.replace("${WARNING_FLAGS}", "")
        return len(cflags_val.strip())

    filtered["_cflags_len"] = filtered.apply(cflags_length, axis=1)
    filtered = filtered.sort_values("_cflags_len")

    rows_html = []
    for _, row in filtered.iterrows():
        host = row["host"]
        virt_host = virtualization_host_cpu(row["march_native"])
        profile = (row["gentoo_profile"] or "—").replace("default/linux/", "")
        lto = "✓" if row["lto_enabled"] else ""
        pgo = "✓" if row["pgo_enabled"] else ""
        graphite = "✓" if row["graphite_enabled"] else ""

        # Expand template variables in cflags
        cflags_val = row["cflags"] or ""
        cflags_val = cflags_val.replace("${COMMON_FLAGS}", row["common_flags"] or "")
        cflags_val = cflags_val.replace("${WARNING_FLAGS}", "")
        cflags_expanded = cflags_val.strip() if cflags_val.strip() else "—"

        rows_html.append(
            "<tr>"
            f"<td>{escape(str(host))}</td>"
            f"<td>{escape(str(virt_host))}</td>"
            f"<td>{escape(str(profile))}</td>"
            f"<td class='opt-col'>{lto}</td>"
            f"<td class='opt-col'>{pgo}</td>"
            f"<td class='opt-col'>{graphite}</td>"
            f"<td class='cflags-col'><code>{escape(cflags_expanded)}</code></td>"
            "</tr>"
        )

    return (
        "<div class='gentoo-config-table-wrap'>"
        "<table class='table table-sm gentoo-config-table'>"
        "<colgroup>"
        "<col><col><col><col class='opt-col'><col class='opt-col'><col class='opt-col'><col>"
        "</colgroup>"
        "<thead><tr>"
        "<th>Host</th><th>Virtualization Host CPU</th><th>Profile</th>"
        "<th class='opt-col'>LTO</th><th class='opt-col'>PGO</th>"
        "<th class='opt-col'>Graphite</th><th class='cflags-col'>CFLAGS</th>"
        "</tr></thead>"
        f"<tbody>{''.join(rows_html)}</tbody>"
        "</table>"
        "</div>"
    )

if not gentoo_hosts.empty:
    from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

    # Display Intel Alder Lake hosts
    alder_lake_table = build_table_for_arch(gentoo_hosts, "alderlake")
    if alder_lake_table:
        display(Markdown("### Intel Alder Lake"))
        display(HTML(alder_lake_table))

    # Display Intel Coffee Lake hosts (detected as skylake by gcc)
    coffee_lake_table = build_table_for_arch(gentoo_hosts, "skylake")
    if coffee_lake_table:
        display(Markdown("### Intel Coffee Lake"))
        display(HTML(coffee_lake_table))

    # Display other architectures
    for arch in sorted(gentoo_hosts["march_native"].unique()):
        if arch not in ["alderlake", "skylake"]:
            arch_table = build_table_for_arch(gentoo_hosts, arch)
            if arch_table:
                arch_name = _translate_march_to_codename(arch)
                display(Markdown(f"### {arch_name}"))
                display(HTML(arch_table))
```

## Cross-OS Comparison (Lower is Better)

```{python}
host_median = (
    df.groupby(["host", "os", "os_family"], as_index=False)["mean_s"]
    .median()
    .rename(columns={"mean_s": "median_seconds"})
    .sort_values("median_seconds")
)

fig = px.bar(
    host_median,
    x="host",
    y="median_seconds",
    color="os_family",
    title="Median benchmark runtime per host",
    labels={"median_seconds": "Median runtime (seconds)", "host": "Host"},
)
fig.update_layout(xaxis_tickangle=-35)
fig
```

## Category-Normalized Performance Heatmap

```{python}
cat_host = (
    df.groupby(["category", "host", "os_family"], as_index=False)["mean_s"]
    .median()
    .rename(columns={"mean_s": "median_s"})
)
cat_host["best_in_category"] = cat_host.groupby("category")["median_s"].transform("min")
cat_host["relative_to_best"] = cat_host["median_s"] / cat_host["best_in_category"]

pivot = cat_host.pivot(index="category", columns="host", values="relative_to_best")

fig = px.imshow(
    pivot,
    aspect="auto",
    color_continuous_scale="Viridis",
    labels={"color": "Relative runtime (1.0 = best)", "x": "Host", "y": "Category"},
    title="Category-normalized runtime by host",
)
fig
```

::: {.metric-callout}
Interpretation guide:

- Values lower than peers indicate faster execution for this benchmark corpus.
- The tuning profile chart is causal **hypothesis support**, not proof; host hardware, package versions,
  and enabled benchmark categories can also drive differences.
- Use per-category sections to confirm whether improvements are broad or concentrated.
:::

## Per-Category Deep Dives

Each category section starts with a description of what the workload measures and why it matters,
followed by a cross-OS comparison chart, a Gentoo-specific tuning chart, and qualitative
interpretation. **All stored metrics are wall-clock times in seconds** (from Hyperfine), so
**lower is always better** for every chart below.  Where a benchmark conceptually measures
*throughput* (e.g. crypto MB/s, memory bandwidth), the note in each section explains the
relationship between the stored time and the underlying throughput concept.

```{python}
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

category_names = sorted(df["category"].dropna().unique())


def describe_series(series, label, unit_label: str, lower_is_better: bool = True):
    stddev = series.std(ddof=1)
    stddev_text = f"{stddev:.3f}{unit_label}" if pd.notna(stddev) else "n/a"
    best_val = series.min() if lower_is_better else series.max()
    worst_val = series.max() if lower_is_better else series.min()
    return (
        f"{label}: best **{best_val:.3f}{unit_label}**, worst **{worst_val:.3f}{unit_label}**, "
        f"median **{series.median():.3f}{unit_label}**, stddev **{stddev_text}**"
    )


def describe_host_outliers(category_frame, unit_label: str):
    host_medians = (
        category_frame.groupby("host", as_index=False)["mean_s"]
        .median()
        .rename(columns={"mean_s": "median_s"})
    )
    mean_median = float(host_medians["median_s"].mean())
    std_median = float(host_medians["median_s"].std(ddof=1))
    if pd.isna(std_median) or std_median == 0.0:
        return (
            f"Across hosts, the mean of host medians is **{mean_median:.3f}{unit_label}** and no "
            "statistically meaningful outliers are present."
        )

    host_medians["zscore"] = (host_medians["median_s"] - mean_median) / std_median
    outliers = host_medians[host_medians["zscore"].abs() >= 2.0].sort_values("zscore")
    if outliers.empty:
        return (
            f"Across hosts, the mean of host medians is **{mean_median:.3f}{unit_label}** with stddev "
            f"**{std_median:.3f}{unit_label}**; no host is more than 2 standard deviations from the mean."
        )

    parts = []
    for _idx, row in outliers.iterrows():
        direction = "above" if row["zscore"] > 0 else "below"
        parts.append(
            f"`{row['host']}` ({row['median_s']:.3f}{unit_label}, {row['zscore']:.1f}σ {direction} mean)"
        )
    return (
        f"Across hosts, the mean of host medians is **{mean_median:.3f}{unit_label}** with stddev "
        f"**{std_median:.3f}{unit_label}**; extreme outliers: {'; '.join(parts)}."
    )


for category in category_names:
    cat_df = df[df["category"] == category].copy()
    if cat_df.empty:
        display(Markdown(f"### {category.replace('_', ' ').title()}"))
        display(Markdown("*No data available for this category.*"))
        continue

    meta = get_category_meta(category)

    cat_df["os_display"] = cat_df.apply(
        lambda row: row["distro_label"] if str(row.get("distro_label", "")).strip() else row["os"],
        axis=1,
    )

    display(Markdown(f"### {meta.title}"))

    # Workload description from catalog
    display(Markdown(
        f"::: {{.callout-note}}\n"
        f"**What this measures:** {meta.description}\n"
        f":::"
    ))

    display(
        Markdown(
            f"Metric direction: **{meta.direction_note}** (stored as wall-clock seconds). "
            "The coverage table below is sorted by host-level median. The OS-level winner is "
            "determined by per-OS median of raw `mean_s` values. The virtualization host CPU "
            "is shown inline so hardware-sourced effects remain visible."
        )
    )

    cat_df["virt_host_cpu"] = cat_df["march_native"].apply(virtualization_host_cpu)

    coverage = (
        cat_df.groupby(["os_display", "host", "virt_host_cpu"], as_index=False)
        .agg(
            benchmarks=("benchmark", "nunique"),
            samples=("mean_s", "count"),
            median_s=("mean_s", "median"),
            stddev_s=("stddev_s", "median"),
        )
        .sort_values(
            ["median_s", "os_display", "host"],
            ascending=[meta.sort_ascending, True, True],
        )
    )
    coverage = coverage.rename(
        columns={
            "os_display": "Operating System",
            "virt_host_cpu": "Virtualization Host CPU",
            "benchmarks": "Benchmarks",
            "samples": "Samples",
            "median_s": "Median_s",
            "stddev_s": "Stddev_s",
        }
    )
    display(Markdown("**Coverage and central tendency**"))
    display(HTML(coverage.to_html(index=False, classes="table table-sm coverage-table")))

    os_median = (
        cat_df.groupby("os_display", as_index=False)["mean_s"]
        .median()
        .rename(columns={"mean_s": "median_s"})
        .sort_values("median_s", ascending=meta.sort_ascending)
    )

    # For time metrics: best=lowest (iloc[0]), worst=highest (iloc[-1])
    # For rate metrics: best=highest (iloc[0] after desc sort), worst=lowest (iloc[-1])
    best_os = os_median.iloc[0]["os_display"]
    worst_os = os_median.iloc[-1]["os_display"]
    best_val = float(os_median.iloc[0]["median_s"])
    worst_val = float(os_median.iloc[-1]["median_s"])
    if meta.lower_is_better:
        spread = (worst_val / best_val) if best_val > 0 else float("nan")
    else:
        spread = (best_val / worst_val) if worst_val > 0 else float("nan")

    fig_os = px.bar(
        os_median,
        x="os_display",
        y="median_s",
        title=f"{meta.title}: Median {meta.unit_label} by OS ({meta.direction_note})",
        labels={"os_display": "Operating system", "median_s": meta.y_axis_label},
    )
    fig_os.update_layout(xaxis_tickangle=-30)
    display(fig_os)

    display(
        Markdown(
            f"**Cross-OS interpretation ({meta.direction_note}, OS-level median):** "
            f"`{best_os}` is currently {meta.winner_label} in this category "
            f"(median **{best_val:.3f}{meta.unit_label}**), while `{worst_os}` is at the other end "
            f"(median **{worst_val:.3f}{meta.unit_label}**), a spread of about **{spread:.2f}×**."
        )
    )
    display(
        Markdown(
            describe_series(
                cat_df.loc[cat_df["os_display"] == best_os, "mean_s"],
                f"{meta.winner_label.capitalize()} OS `{best_os}` sample distribution",
                meta.unit_label,
                lower_is_better=meta.lower_is_better,
            )
        )
    )
    display(Markdown(describe_host_outliers(cat_df, meta.unit_label)))

    gentoo_cat = cat_df[cat_df["os"] == "Gentoo"].copy()
    if not gentoo_cat.empty:
        gentoo_cat["tuning_profile"] = (
            np.where(gentoo_cat["lto_enabled"], "LTO:on", "LTO:off")
            + " | "
            + np.where(gentoo_cat["pgo_enabled"], "PGO:on", "PGO:off")
            + " | "
            + np.where(gentoo_cat["graphite_enabled"], "Graphite:on", "Graphite:off")
        )

        fig_gentoo = px.box(
            gentoo_cat,
            x="host",
            y="mean_s",
            color="tuning_profile",
            title=f"{meta.title}: Gentoo host distribution by tuning profile ({meta.direction_note})",
            labels={"host": "Gentoo host", "mean_s": meta.y_axis_label},
            points="all",
        )
        fig_gentoo.update_layout(xaxis_tickangle=-30)
        display(fig_gentoo)

        tuning_median = (
            gentoo_cat.groupby("tuning_profile", as_index=False)["mean_s"]
            .median()
            .rename(columns={"mean_s": "median_s"})
            .sort_values("median_s", ascending=meta.sort_ascending)
        )
        best_tuning = tuning_median.iloc[0]["tuning_profile"]
        best_tuning_val = float(tuning_median.iloc[0]["median_s"])
        display(
            Markdown(
                f"**Gentoo tuning interpretation ({meta.direction_note}, host-level median):** "
                f"The {meta.winner_label} result in this category comes from "
                f"**{best_tuning}** at **{best_tuning_val:.3f}{meta.unit_label}**. Compare this against "
                "compile-time cost and maintainability before treating it as globally optimal."
            )
        )
        display(
            Markdown(
                describe_series(
                    gentoo_cat.loc[gentoo_cat["tuning_profile"] == best_tuning, "mean_s"],
                    f"{meta.winner_label.capitalize()} tuning `{best_tuning}` sample distribution",
                    meta.unit_label,
                    lower_is_better=meta.lower_is_better,
                )
            )
        )
    else:
        display(
            Markdown(
                "**Gentoo tuning interpretation:** No Gentoo rows are available in this "
                "category for detailed tuning-level comparison."
            )
        )

    # Analysis hint from catalog
    display(Markdown(
        f"::: {{.callout-tip}}\n"
        f"**Analysis hint:** {meta.analysis_hint}\n"
        f":::"
    ))

    display(
        Markdown(
            "**Caveats:** Category-level winners are not universal winners. Hardware "
            "differences, package versions, microarchitecture behavior, and benchmark command "
            "mix can shift results. Use this deep-dive together with compile-time and "
            "maintenance trade-offs before choosing production defaults."
        )
    )
```

## Gentoo CFLAGS Deep-Dive

The analysis below focuses specifically on Gentoo hosts, breaking down the impact of key CFLAGS
dimensions (`-march` class, optimization level, LTO, PGO, and Graphite) on performance across
all benchmark categories. This section enriches the benchmark data with normalized CFLAGS parsing
to extract these dimensions from the original metadata.

```{python}
# Enrich Gentoo dataframe with normalized CFLAGS dimensions
gentoo_df = df[df["os"] == "Gentoo"].copy()
if not gentoo_df.empty:
    gentoo_df = enrich_gentoo_cflags_dimensions(gentoo_df)
else:
    # Still initialize columns even if empty (for consistency)
    gentoo_df["march_class"] = "unknown"
    gentoo_df["opt_level"] = "unknown"
    gentoo_df["lto_mode"] = "unknown"
    gentoo_df["pgo_mode"] = "unknown"
    gentoo_df["graphite_mode"] = "unknown"

display(Markdown("### CFLAGS Coverage by Host and Dimension"))

# Create coverage table: hosts × dimension values
if not gentoo_df.empty:
    coverage_parts = []
    for host in sorted(gentoo_df["host"].unique()):
        host_data = gentoo_df[gentoo_df["host"] == host]
        coverage_parts.append({
            "Host": host,
            "march_class": ", ".join(sorted(set(host_data["march_class"].dropna().unique()))),
            "opt_level": ", ".join(sorted(set(host_data["opt_level"].dropna().unique()))),
            "lto_mode": ", ".join(sorted(set(host_data["lto_mode"].dropna().unique()))),
            "pgo_mode": ", ".join(sorted(set(host_data["pgo_mode"].dropna().unique()))),
            "graphite_mode": ", ".join(sorted(set(host_data["graphite_mode"].dropna().unique()))),
        })
    
    coverage_table = pd.DataFrame(coverage_parts)
    display(Markdown("**Host × Dimension Coverage:**"))
    display(HTML(coverage_table.to_html(index=False, classes="table table-sm coverage-table")))
    
    display(Markdown("### Aggregate Effect Charts by Dimension"))
    
    # For each dimension, show median benchmark results by dimension value
    dimensions = ["march_class", "opt_level", "lto_mode", "pgo_mode", "graphite_mode"]
    
    for dim in dimensions:
        dim_display_name = dim.replace("_", " ").title()
        display(Markdown(f"#### {dim_display_name}"))
        
        # Aggregate medians across all samples by dimension value
        dim_medians = (
            gentoo_df.groupby(dim, as_index=False)["mean_s"]
            .median()
            .rename(columns={"mean_s": "median_s"})
            .sort_values("median_s")
        )
        dim_medians = dim_medians.rename(columns={dim: "Value"})
        
        if not dim_medians.empty:
            fig = px.bar(
                dim_medians,
                x="Value",
                y="median_s",
                title=f"Median benchmark time by {dim_display_name}",
                labels={"median_s": "Median time (seconds)", "Value": dim_display_name},
            )
            fig.update_layout(xaxis_tickangle=-30)
            display(fig)
            
            # Add brief interpretation
            best_val = dim_medians.iloc[0]["Value"]
            best_time = float(dim_medians.iloc[0]["median_s"])
            worst_val = dim_medians.iloc[-1]["Value"]
            worst_time = float(dim_medians.iloc[-1]["median_s"])
            spread = (worst_time / best_time) if best_time > 0 else 1.0
            
            display(Markdown(
                f"**{dim_display_name} Summary:** Best performing value is "
                f"`{best_val}` (median **{best_time:.3f}s**), "
                f"while `{worst_val}` is slowest (median **{worst_time:.3f}s**), "
                f"a spread of approximately **{spread:.2f}×**."
            ))
        else:
            display(Markdown(f"*No data available for {dim_display_name}.*"))
    
    display(Markdown("### Per-Category Dimension Effects"))
    
    # Create heatmap showing which dimensions most affect which categories
    display(Markdown(
        "The heatmap below shows the spread (ratio of slowest to fastest) for each "
        "dimension within each category. Higher values indicate greater impact of that dimension on that category."
    ))
    
    heatmap_data = []
    categories = sorted(gentoo_df["category"].dropna().unique())
    
    for category in categories:
        cat_data = gentoo_df[gentoo_df["category"] == category]
        for dim in dimensions:
            dim_groups = cat_data.groupby(dim)["mean_s"].median()
            if len(dim_groups) > 1:
                min_val = dim_groups.min()
                max_val = dim_groups.max()
                spread = (max_val / min_val) if min_val > 0 else 1.0
            else:
                spread = 1.0
            heatmap_data.append({
                "Category": category.replace("_", " ").title(),
                "Dimension": dim.replace("_", " ").title(),
                "Spread": spread
            })
    
    if heatmap_data:
        heatmap_df = pd.DataFrame(heatmap_data)
        pivot_heatmap = heatmap_df.pivot(index="Category", columns="Dimension", values="Spread")
        
        fig = px.imshow(
            pivot_heatmap,
            aspect="auto",
            color_continuous_scale="YlOrRd",
            labels={"color": "Spread (max/min)"},
            title="CFLAGS Dimension Impact on Benchmark Categories (spread ratio)",
        )
        display(fig)
    
    display(Markdown("### Interpretation and Caveats"))
    
    display(Markdown("""
::: {.callout-warning}
**Key Caveats:**

- **Confounders:** The dimension values are not orthogonal—hosts with `-march=native` may also differ in 
  optimization level, LTO, PGO, or Graphite settings. This analysis shows *association*, not causation.
  
- **Stability:** Benchmark results are influenced by hardware (CPU, cache, thermal throttling), system load,
  kernel version, package versions, and other factors beyond CFLAGS.
  
- **Limited sample size:** If a host uses only one value for a dimension (e.g., all samples have `lto_mode=off`),
  that dimension cannot be evaluated within that host.
  
- **Category bias:** Some categories may be more sensitive to certain optimizations (e.g., crypto to LTO),
  while others show little variation.
  
- **Interaction effects:** The combined effect of multiple flags may not be the sum of individual effects.

**Conclusion:** Use these results to form hypotheses about which dimensions *might* affect your workload,
then validate by profiling on representative hardware with controlled experiments.
:::
"""))
else:
    display(Markdown("*No Gentoo data available for CFLAGS deep-dive analysis.*"))
```
